# How to Book KTX Train Tickets in Korea as a Foreigner

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/how-to-book-ktx-korea/
Last checked: 2026-10-23

## Quick answer

- Book in English on Korail's official site for foreigners (korail.com/global/eng) or in the KORAIL+ app. The normal booking window opens at 07:00 (Korea time) two months before your travel date; Seollal and Chuseok holiday trains follow a separate schedule.
- KTX and SRT merged on September 1, 2026. The government says they now run as KTX, with fares on average 10% lower than before. Seoul–Busan (via Gyeongju) is ₩54,400 in standard class.
- Keep your email and password — that's how you look up a ticket booked on the foreigner site, and you'll need them to cancel online before departure.

![A blue KTX-Cheongryong high-speed train waiting at a platform at Seoul Station](/img/photo-ktx-seoul-station.jpg?v=326e9396 "A KTX-Cheongryong train at Seoul Station, 2024. Photo: 생각하는 나무 (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

The KTX is Korea's high-speed train, and you can book it in English before you arrive. There's one change you won't find in older guides: on September 1, 2026, the KTX and the SRT — the high-speed trains that used to run from Suseo Station under a separate company — started running as one service called KTX. So if a blog post sends you to a separate SRT website, it's out of date.

## The short version

| | What to know |
|---|---|
| Where to book | Korail's site for foreigners (korail.com/global/eng), the KORAIL+ app, ticket machines or station counters — not at subway stations |
| When tickets go on sale | Normally from 07:00 (Korea time), two months before your travel date — holiday trains differ |
| How to pay | Credit card (online) |
| Finding your ticket | The email address and password you used when booking |
| Cancelling | Online before departure; after departure, generally at a station counter (see the KORAIL+ exception below) |

Source: [Korail — ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets) and [purchase and refund guide](https://www.korail.com/ticket/reserve/guide/pay) (Korean); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## What changed in September 2026

Korea used to have two high-speed operators: Korail ran the KTX, and a separate company, SR, ran the SRT from Suseo Station. After the companies were merged, the government says the two started running as KTX from September 1, 2026. Three things matter for visitors:

- **One place to book.** Integrated trains are booked through the KORAIL+ app and the Korail website. KORAIL+ replaced Korail's old app, Korail Talk.
- **Lower fares.** The government says KTX fares were brought down to former SRT levels — about 10% lower on average.
- **More seats on trains from Suseo.** Most of the added trains run on the Suseo routes, which the government says have about 30% more seats.

Source: [Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Aug 31, 2026](https://www.korea.kr/news/policyNewsView.do?newsId=148970889) and [Aug 3, 2026](https://www.korea.kr/news/policyNewsView.do?newsId=148969267) (Korean); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## How much a KTX ticket costs

These are adult standard-class fares from Korail's official KTX fare table, effective September 1, 2026:

| Route | Standard class |
|---|---|
| Seoul – Busan (via Gyeongju) | ₩54,400 |
| Suseo – Busan | ₩52,900 |
| Seoul – Dongdaegu (Daegu) | ₩39,000 |
| Seoul – Gyeongju | ₩44,500 |
| Seoul – Daejeon | ₩21,600 |
| Yongsan – Gwangju Songjeong | ₩42,000 |
| Yongsan – Jeonju | ₩31,600 |
| Yongsan – Yeosu EXPO | ₩45,400 |

Fares vary by route — the same two cities can have different fares depending on the stops a train makes — so check the price shown when you book. Korail's table also notes that the 10% reduction was set for three years and may be adjusted later.

![Rows of grey standard-class seats inside a KTX-Cheongryong carriage](/img/photo-ktx-standard-class.jpg?v=b1b9743d "Standard class on a KTX-Cheongryong train, 2024. Photo: 생각하는 나무 (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

Source: [Korail — KTX fare table, as of Sep 1, 2026](https://www.korail.com/ticket/reserve/train-timeTable) (Korean, Excel download); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Booking online, in English

![Booking a KTX ticket in four steps: open Korail's English site or the KORAIL+ app, search, save your email and password, pay by credit card](/img/ktx-steps.png?v=a7f9ef86 "Booking in four steps. Details below.")

1. Go to **korail.com/global/eng** — Korail's official site for foreigners. (The old letskorail.com address now redirects to korail.com.)
2. Search your departure station, arrival station, date and number of passengers, and pick a train.
3. Enter an email address and a password. Korail says you need to type them exactly — including upper- and lower-case letters — to look up your ticket later, and suggests writing them down.
4. Pay by credit card.
5. To check or cancel, open **MY TICKET** and enter the same email and password.

Source: [Korail — official site for foreigners](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/main) and [ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Save the email and password in your phone's notes the moment you book. Without them you can't pull up the ticket on the foreigner site.

## When tickets go on sale

Korail says the normal booking window opens at **07:00 (Korea time), two months before** the departure date. Online, you can buy until the train leaves; ticket machines stop selling 10 minutes before departure, and station counters sell until departure.

The big exception is Korea's two main holidays. Seollal and Chuseok holiday trains can have their own reservation schedule and rules — for Chuseok 2026, Korail ran a separate booking period that required membership, then opened remaining seats later, when non-members could buy and pay straight away. Check Korail's latest holiday notice if you're travelling around those dates.

> **Our take:** For Friday-to-Sunday trips, book as soon as your normal booking window opens. Those are also the days with higher cancellation fees, so pick your train with care.

Source: [Korail — ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets) and [2026 Chuseok reservations notice](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/siteInfo/notice/25622); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Buying at the station

![Korail ticket counters, ticket machines and departure boards at Pyeongtaek Station](/img/photo-korail-ticket-counter.jpg?v=00f643af "Korail ticket counters and machines at Pyeongtaek Station, 2024. Photo: MNXANL (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

You can also buy at ticket machines or the counter in a train station. Note that this means a railway station — Korail says KTX tickets aren't sold at subway stations.

Source: [Korail — ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## If your plans change

Before departure, you can cancel online — in MY TICKET for tickets booked on Korail's English website. After the train has left, the English guide directs you to a station counter. Korail's Korean guide also lists an exception: KTX tickets bought through KORAIL+ can be refunded in the app up to 10 minutes after departure, if it's confirmed that you're not on the train. Follow the refund options for the channel you bought from. Refunds aren't possible after the arrival time printed on the ticket.

The fee depends on when you cancel and on the day of travel. "The day before" means the previous calendar date, not a rolling 24-hour period:

| When you cancel | Mon–Thu trains (excluding public holidays and designated holiday periods) | Fri–Sun, public holidays, Seollal and Chuseok |
|---|---|---|
| From booking until 2 days before departure | No fee | Minimum fee |
| The day before departure | No fee | 5% |
| On the departure date, until 3 hours before | No fee | 10% |
| Less than 3 hours before departure | 5% | 20% |
| Up to 20 minutes after departure | 15% | 30% |
| 20 to 60 minutes after departure | 40% | 40% |
| 60 minutes after departure until arrival | 70% | 70% |

Korail's Korean guide lists the minimum fee as ₩400.

Source: [Korail — purchase and refund guide](https://www.korail.com/ticket/reserve/guide/pay) (Korean) and [ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Is the KORAIL PASS worth it?

The KORAIL PASS is a rail pass for foreign visitors. The current select passes let you choose 2, 3, 4 or 5 travel days within a 10-day period from the pass's starting date:

| Pass | Adult (13+) | Child (6–12) |
|---|---|---|
| 2-day select | ₩131,000 | ₩66,000 |
| 3-day select | ₩186,000 | ₩93,000 |
| 4-day select | ₩234,000 | ₩117,000 |
| 5-day select | ₩275,000 | ₩138,000 |

You need a valid passport and a credit card to buy it, and the details must match your passport. Choose your travel dates in MY TICKET before reserving seats; seat reservations open two months before departure, up to two seat tickets per person per day. Board with your pass, your passport and, if you reserved one, your seat reservation. Refunds are possible only before the pass's starting date.

Korail's current pass guide lists metropolitan railways and temporary tourist trains as not included. An older notice from 2024 also excluded SRT trains, which have run as KTX since September 2026. If your plans use trains from Suseo Station, check that a seat reservation is available for that train when you book, or ask Korail's call center (+82-1599-7777).

Source: [Korail — About KORAIL PASS](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/korailpass), [pass reservation](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/korailpass/reservation) and [older pass notice](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/siteInfo/notice/18801); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Our take:** Do the sums for your own trip. A 2-day pass costs ₩131,000, while a Seoul–Busan return in standard class is ₩108,800 (₩54,400 each way via Gyeongju) — so for one return trip, regular tickets are cheaper. A pass can make sense when you're fitting several long trips into a short window.

## Before you travel

1. Decide your stations — trains to Busan leave from Seoul Station and Suseo Station, among others.
2. Book from 07:00 (Korea time) two months ahead for weekend trips — and check Korail's holiday notice if you're travelling around Seollal or Chuseok.
3. Save your booking email and password.
4. Check you'll have data on the day for the app or your ticket — see [eSIM vs SIM card vs pocket Wi-Fi](/esim-sim-card-pocket-wifi-korea/).
5. Plan the trip to the station: [how to use Naver Map](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/) and [how to get a T-money card](/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/).

## FAQ

### Can foreigners book KTX tickets online?

Yes. Korail runs an English site for foreigners at korail.com/global/eng, and tickets can also be bought in the KORAIL+ app, at ticket machines and at station counters.

### How far in advance can I book the KTX?

Korail's normal booking window opens at 07:00 (Korea time), two months before the departure date. Seollal and Chuseok holiday trains can follow a separate schedule.

### How much is the KTX from Seoul to Busan?

₩54,400 for an adult in standard class from Seoul Station via Gyeongju, and ₩52,900 from Suseo Station, according to Korail's fare table effective September 1, 2026. Other routes between the two cities can cost a different amount.

### Is the SRT still separate from the KTX?

No. The government says the KTX and SRT started running as one KTX service on September 1, 2026, with integrated trains booked through KORAIL+ and the Korail website.

### Can I get a refund on a KTX ticket?

Yes. Before departure you can cancel online; after departure, generally at a station counter (KORAIL+ KTX tickets can be refunded in the app up to 10 minutes after departure if you're not on the train). No refunds after arrival. Fees depend on timing and the day of travel. For non-holiday Monday–Thursday departures, cancellation more than three hours before departure is free. Public holidays and the designated Seollal/Chuseok travel periods use the holiday fee schedule.

## Sources

# Paying in Korea: Foreign Cards, Cash and What Still Needs Won

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/paying-in-korea-foreign-cards-cash/
Last checked: 2026-10-23

## Quick answer

- Credit cards are widely used — the Korea Tourism Organization names Visa, Mastercard and American Express — but check that each shop accepts your card, and carry some won for cash-only needs.
- Carry a little won anyway. A regular T-money card is topped up with Korean won cash.
- Landing at Incheon Terminal 1? The arrivals floor has currency exchange counters that are open 24 hours.

Cards are widely used in Korea. Hotels, department stores and most shops take them, and taxis accept card payment too — though no one can promise your particular card will work everywhere. The catch is the small stuff — a regular T-money top-up, the odd shop that doesn't take cards — and that's where a little Korean won saves you a walk to the ATM.

![Where a foreign card works in Korea: shops and hotels usually, taxis usually, new subway ticket machines yes with a fee, regular T-money top-ups at stores or stations need won cash](/img/pay-compare.png?v=96e100e5 "Card or cash? Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| Where | Foreign card? | Good to know |
|---|---|---|
| Hotels, department stores, most shops | Usually | Some stores don't take cards — check before you buy |
| Taxis | Usually — check before you get in | Cash, credit card or a transport card |
| Subway single tickets and Climate Card short-term passes | Yes, at the 440 new machines on Lines 1–8 | About 3.7% service fee |
| Topping up a regular T-money card at a store or station | No | Korean won cash |
| TABA taxi app | Yes | Visa, Mastercard, UnionPay, JCB |

Source: [VISITKOREA — currency](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140040) and [taxis](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140661); [Seoul Metropolitan Government](https://english.seoul.go.kr/climate-cards-and-single-journey-transit-tickets-now-accepting-international-credit-cards-no-cash-needed/); [T-money](https://pay.tmoney.co.kr/ncs/pct/ugd/ReadFrgnGd.dev); [TABA](https://www.tabataxi.app/); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Paying by card

The Korea Tourism Organization puts it simply: most businesses in Korea accept credit cards, from major hotels and department stores to general shops, and Visa, Mastercard and American Express can be used. It also adds a caution worth taking seriously — some stores don't provide card payment, so check before you buy.

Taxis are usually straightforward: VISITKOREA says passengers can pay with cash, a credit card or a transportation card. That's a general rule, not a promise that a particular foreign-issued card will go through, so it's worth checking as you get in.

Source: [VISITKOREA — Korean Currency & Exchange Info](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140040); [VISITKOREA — Taxis](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140661) (updated Jan 2026); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Where won still comes in handy

![Street-food stalls and shoppers on Myeongdong 7-gil in Seoul in the early evening](/img/photo-myeongdong-street-food.jpg?v=71464c29 "Myeongdong 7-gil, Seoul, 2023. Photo: SKTakek (CC0), cropped.")

The clearest case for cash is a regular T-money card topped up at a store or station. T-money's guide for visitors says you top it up by handing over the card and Korean won cash at a T-money sales location.

The subway itself has got easier. Since March 17, 2026, the 440 new ticket machines at 273 stations on Seoul Subway Lines 1–8 accept international cards such as Visa and Mastercard — for single-journey tickets and Climate Card short-term passes. Expect a service fee of about 3.7%. The former 30-day Climate Card pass is no longer available for top-up; the 1-, 2-, 3-, 5- and 7-day short-term passes continue to operate.

So if your plan is a T-money card, land with some won. If you'd rather carry as little cash as possible, the Climate Card short-term pass or single tickets are the card-friendly route on the subway.

Source: [T-money — guide for foreign visitors](https://pay.tmoney.co.kr/ncs/pct/ugd/ReadFrgnGd.dev); [Seoul Metropolitan Government](https://english.seoul.go.kr/climate-cards-and-single-journey-transit-tickets-now-accepting-international-credit-cards-no-cash-needed/) and [Seoul transport news](https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/archives/516544) (Korean), Mar 2026; and [Climate Card 30-day end-of-service FAQ](https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/public/climatecard-faq/faq-stop) (Korean); checked Oct 23, 2026. More on the card itself: [how to get a T-money card](/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/).

## Getting won when you land

VISITKOREA's advice is that for most tourists, the airport exchange centers are the easiest place to change money.

At Incheon Airport Terminal 1, the arrivals floor (1F) has:

- **24-hour exchange counters** — Woori Bank near Exits 6 and 11, and KB Bank near Arrival Hall B
- **Exchange counters open 06:00–22:00** — Hana Bank near Exit 4 and KB Bank near Exit 9
- **24-hour ATMs** near Exits 4, 6, 9 and 11

The airport's directory doesn't say which ATMs take foreign-issued cards, so look at the card logos on the machine before you put your card in. This list is for Terminal 1; check the airport's facility search if you arrive at Terminal 2.

In town, banks are generally open 09:00–16:00 on weekdays, and Korea Post Bank 09:00–16:30. Hours vary by branch, and some places won't exchange old banknotes.

Source: [VISITKOREA FAQ](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/faq/faqMainView.do?menuSn=404&pstSn=95); [Incheon Airport — Convenience & Public Facilities](https://www.airport.kr/ap_en/1536/subview.do); [VISITKOREA — currency](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140040); checked Oct 23, 2026. Getting into the city: [Incheon Airport to Seoul](/incheon-airport-to-seoul/).

> **Local tip:** Before you fly, check two things with your bank: that your card is set up for use abroad, and what it charges for foreign transactions and cash withdrawals. It's easier to sort out at home than at an ATM at midnight.

## Taxi apps and NAVER's visitor verification

**TABA** is a taxi app for travelers. Its official site says you can pay with Visa, Mastercard, China UnionPay, JCB and more, sign up with an international phone number, and that it works officially with the Seoul Metropolitan Government and T-money.

**NAVER** introduced Passport Verification on June 4, 2026, so eligible foreign visitors can verify their identity for supported booking and ordering services without a Korean mobile number. This is separate from payment approval. NAVER's Booking/Order help lists supported overseas card networks, while some Npay services are restricted to Npay Korea Members. Check the payment options shown for your booking before relying on a particular card. (If you're still choosing how to get online, see [eSIM vs SIM card vs pocket Wi-Fi](/esim-sim-card-pocket-wifi-korea/) — and [how to use Naver Map](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/).)

Source: [TABA](https://www.tabataxi.app/); [NAVER press release, Jun 9, 2026](https://www.navercorp.com/en/media/pressReleasesDetail?seq=10034413); NAVER Help — [passport verification](https://help.naver.com/service/5640/contents/25235?lang=ko&osType=COMMONOS), [supported cards](https://help.naver.com/service/11713/contents/24272?lang=en&osType=COMMONOS) and [Npay Korea Member restrictions](https://help.naver.com/service/11713/contents/24269?lang=en&osType=COMMONOS); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Prepaid travel cards

Some visitors use a prepaid card made for travelers. WOWPASS is one: its maker, Orange Square, describes it as an all-in-one prepaid card for foreign travelers covering money exchange, payment and transportation, and says you verify ownership in its app to withdraw a remaining balance in cash. Fees and limits change, so check the current terms in the app before you buy.

Source: [WOWPASS App Store listing (Orange Square, Inc)](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/wowpass-go-cashless-in-korea/id1626691440); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Our take

![Inside Gwangjang Market in Seoul: food stalls with Korean signs under strings of flags](/img/photo-gwangjang-market.jpg?v=aa69a454 "Gwangjang Market, Seoul, 2022. Photo: Bgag (CC0), cropped.")

> **Our take:** Plan to pay by card, but don't arrive with zero won. A small amount covers a T-money top-up and the occasional place that doesn't take cards, and it saves you hunting for an ATM at the wrong moment. If you'd rather skip cash on the subway, use the new ticket machines and accept the fee.

## Before you fly

1. Tell your bank you're travelling and check its foreign transaction and ATM fees.
2. Bring a backup card, kept separately from your main one.
3. Decide on your transit card — T-money (top up with won cash) or the Climate Card short-term pass (card-friendly at the new machines in Seoul).
4. Note where the 24-hour exchange counters are if you land late at Incheon Terminal 1.

## FAQ

### Can I use my foreign credit card in Korea?

Cards are widely used. The Korea Tourism Organization says Visa, Mastercard and American Express can be used, from hotels and department stores to general shops, but some stores don't take cards — check that each place accepts yours.

### Do I need cash in Korea?

A little. Topping up a regular T-money card at a store or station takes Korean won cash, and some shops don't accept cards.

### Can I buy Seoul subway tickets with a foreign card?

Yes, since March 17, 2026, at the 440 new ticket machines on Lines 1–8 — for single-journey tickets and Climate Card short-term passes, with a service fee of about 3.7%.

### Where can I exchange money at Incheon Airport?

Terminal 1's arrivals floor has 24-hour exchange counters (Woori Bank near Exits 6 and 11, KB Bank near Arrival Hall B), plus counters open 06:00–22:00 near Exits 4 and 9.

### Can I pay by card in a Korean taxi?

Usually. VISITKOREA says taxi passengers can pay with cash, a credit card or a transportation card — check that your card is accepted before you set off.

# eSIM vs SIM Card vs Pocket Wi-Fi in Korea: Which One Should You Get?

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/esim-sim-card-pocket-wifi-korea/
Last checked: 2026-10-22

## Quick answer

- Our pick for most visitors: a data eSIM from a Korean carrier, bought before you fly — if your phone supports eSIM, isn't locked to your home carrier and is on the carrier's supported list. SK Telecom, KT and LG U+ each list one day of LTE data at ₩6,500.
- Need to make calls, or get a text code from a booking app? Check that exact plan before you buy. A Korean number alone isn't enough: KT's data-only eSIM comes with an 010 number that can receive calls and texts after its airport entry check, but outgoing calls and texts need a Data + Voice plan.
- Family or group that stays together? One pocket Wi-Fi (₩4,400 a day at KT and LG U+) covers several phones. You'll have to return it at the airport.

You'll want data from the moment you land. The train timetable, the address of your guesthouse, the map that tells you which station exit to take — you'll be checking them on your phone. There are four ways to get online in Korea, and the right one mostly depends on three things: whether your phone works with the plan you want, whether you need to make calls or get app codes, and whether your group will stay together.

![Comparison of eSIM, physical SIM card, pocket Wi-Fi and free public Wi-Fi in Korea, with prices from the carriers' websites checked Oct 22, 2026](/img/esim-compare.png?v=8092484a "Four ways to get online in Korea. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | Data eSIM | Physical SIM card | Pocket Wi-Fi | Free public Wi-Fi |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| What you get | Data on your own phone | Data, or data + a Korean number | A small router your devices connect to | Free Wi-Fi in public places |
| Price | 1 day ₩6,500 (LTE) | LG U+: same data prices as its eSIM; calls cost extra | ₩4,400 a day | Free |
| Where to get it | Online, then scan a QR code | Airport roaming centers; some convenience stores | Airport counters (reserve online) | Many airports, stations and public places |
| Return it? | No | No | **Yes**, at the airport | — |
| Good for | Solo travelers with an eSIM phone | Phones without eSIM; anyone who needs to make calls | Groups, families, several devices | A backup, not your main connection |

Source: carrier websites — [SK Telecom](https://www.skroaming.com/esim/esim), [KT](https://roaming.kt.com/eng/esim), [LG U+](https://www.lguplus.com/korea-sim/eng/pc/product/esim?tab=data) — and [VISITKOREA](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140041); checked Oct 22, 2026. Prices shown are the carriers' listed KRW prices; check the current total and any discounts before paying.

## First question: data, calls, or app verification?

If you just need maps, messaging apps and the internet, a data-only plan does the job, and you can buy it online before you leave home.

It gets less simple when you think you need "a Korean number". Having a number, receiving calls, making calls and getting a booking app's text code are separate things, and plans differ on each:

- **KT** gives each of its visitor eSIMs an 010 number. With its data-only eSIM you can receive calls and texts after KT's entry check at the airport, but you can't make calls or send texts.
- **LG U+** says text verification for restaurant and taxi booking apps works with its Voice/SMS plans, but not with data only.
- **Calls and texts out** need a Data + Voice plan, switched on after a passport check — LG U+ and KT do this at their airport counters, and KT sells its voice eSIMs at the airport, not online.

So if a particular app matters to you, check that the exact plan supports it before you buy. A local number on its own doesn't mean the code will arrive.

One thing a visitor plan won't do is get you into Korean banking or government services. LG U+ says identity verification for those isn't supported, KT says its eSIM doesn't support personal authentication, and SK Telecom says its 1-day data eSIM can't receive authentication or payment texts.

Source: [LG U+ — SIM card notice](https://www.lguplus.com/korea-sim/eng/pc/product/simcard?tab=data-voice); [KT — eSIM plans](https://roaming.kt.com/eng/esim); [SK Telecom — 1-day data eSIM](https://www.skroaming.com/esim/detail/data-1day); checked Oct 22, 2026.

## What a data eSIM costs

Korea has three major mobile carriers — SK Telecom, KT and LG U+ — and each sells prepaid plans for visitors. Each lists one day of LTE data-only eSIM at ₩6,500. The table compares selected data-only plans; prices for other lengths can differ between carriers.

| Days | KT | LG U+ | SK Telecom |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 day | ₩6,500 | ₩6,500 | ₩6,500 |
| 2 days | ₩12,000 | ₩12,000 | — |
| 3 days | ₩18,000 | ₩18,000 | — |
| 5 days | ₩27,500 | ₩27,500 | — |
| 7 days | ₩35,000 | ₩35,000 | — |
| 10 days | ₩38,500 | ₩38,500 | — |
| 30 days | ₩71,500 | ₩71,500 | — |

On SK Telecom's English eSIM page, the LTE data-only plan we found is the 1-day one; its longer LTE plans come with voice and text (2 days: ₩12,000). A dash means we didn't find a data-only plan of that length, not that the carrier has nothing for your trip. LG U+ shows its longer plans when you tap "more" under the plan lengths.

"Unlimited" means slightly different things. KT gives you 11GB a day at full speed, then up to 5Mbps until it resets at midnight. LG U+ advertises no speed cap, though it says speeds "may be managed" when the network is very busy. SK Telecom's 1-day LTE plan is unlimited at up to 100 Mbps.

Source: [KT — eSIM plans](https://roaming.kt.com/eng/esim); [LG U+ — Korea eSIM](https://www.lguplus.com/korea-sim/eng/pc/product/esim?tab=data); [SK Telecom — eSIM plans](https://www.skroaming.com/esim/esim) and [1-day data eSIM](https://www.skroaming.com/esim/detail/data-1day); checked Oct 22, 2026. Prices shown are the carriers' listed KRW prices. KT and SK Telecom don't accept payment cards issued in Korea on their visitor sites.

## Setting up a Korean eSIM

![Getting a Korean eSIM in four steps: check your phone, buy online, install over Wi-Fi, then switch your data line on arrival](/img/esim-steps.png?v=d03fb5c5 "eSIM setup in four steps. Details below.")

Before you pay, check three things: your phone supports eSIM, it isn't locked to your home carrier, and your exact model is on the Korean carrier's supported list. The third one catches people out. LG U+, for example, currently says its eSIM isn't supported on Google Pixel, Motorola and OPPO devices, and that service may not be available on some phones bought outside Korea. That's a limit of that carrier's plan, so check the device list of the carrier you're buying from.

LG U+ suggests a quick test: dial `*#06#` — if an EID shows up, your phone supports eSIM. Your home carrier can tell you whether the phone is locked.

After you buy, you get a QR code — SK Telecom, for example, sends it in an eSIM voucher by email. Scan it while you're on Wi-Fi or another connection; SK Telecom and LG U+ both say the eSIM needs internet to install or activate.

Then leave it alone. The carriers are blunt about this: delete the eSIM and it can't be restored, so you'd be buying a new one.

Watch the installation deadline, too. LG U+ says to activate within 60 days of purchase. KT's page gives two different deadlines, and its eSIMs can't be refunded, so ask KT which one applies before you pay.

When you land, pick the Korean line for mobile data. On an iPhone that's **Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data**; on Android the menu names depend on the phone maker. If your plan comes with a number, LG U+ notes that it appears after you arrive in Korea.

Source: [SK Telecom — 1-day data eSIM notes](https://www.skroaming.com/esim/detail/data-1day); [LG U+ — Korea eSIM notice](https://www.lguplus.com/korea-sim/eng/pc/product/esim?tab=data); [KT — eSIM plans](https://roaming.kt.com/eng/esim); [Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118227); checked Oct 22, 2026.

> **Local tip:** LG U+ starts counting your days when you first use data, so buying a few days early doesn't eat into your plan. Terms differ by carrier — SK Telecom describes its 1-day plan as 24 hours.

## Buying a physical SIM card

![Arrivals hall of Incheon Airport Terminal 1, seen from the floor above, with travelers and luggage trolleys](/img/photo-icn-t1-arrivals.jpg?v=66c8964f "Incheon Airport Terminal 1 arrivals hall, 2023. Photo: ノボホショコロトソ (CC BY 4.0), cropped.")

No eSIM support? A physical SIM (often called a USIM in Korea) does the same job. Roaming centers at Incheon, Gimpo, Gimhae and Jeju airports sell prepaid SIMs, and you can also buy online and pick up at the airport.

At Incheon Terminal 1, KT has two counters on the arrivals floor (1F): one near Arrival Hall A, open 06:00–22:00, and one near Arrival Hall F that's open 24 hours. Bring your passport. LG U+ switches on plans with calls after a passport check at its airport counter.

![An Emart24 convenience store with a blue awning on a street in Korea](/img/photo-convenience-store.jpg?v=ddebdcc3 "An Emart24 store, 2024. Photo: Sgroey (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

If you skip the airport, VISITKOREA says CU, GS25, 7-Eleven and Emart24 convenience stores sell USIM cards too — but stock varies by branch.

Source: [VISITKOREA — Electricity & Communications](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140041); [LG U+ — Korea SIM Card](https://www.lguplus.com/korea-sim/eng/pc/product/simcard?tab=data-voice); [KT](https://roaming.kt.com/eng/main); checked Oct 22, 2026.

> **Local tip:** When you swap SIMs, tape your home SIM inside your passport cover or put it in a coin pocket. It's tiny, and you'll need it on the way home.

## Renting a pocket Wi-Fi

A pocket Wi-Fi (VISITKOREA calls it a "Wi-Fi egg") is a small battery-powered router. Several phones and laptops can connect at once, which is why families like it. The catch is that it's a rental: you collect it and you return it.

| | KT | LG U+ |
|---|---|---|
| Daily rental | ₩4,400 | ₩4,400 |
| Data | Unlimited at 20Mbps | 4GB a day, then up to 5Mbps |
| Deposit | Credit card in your name, with more than 3 months left before it expires; **debit cards not accepted** for the deposit | Credit card in your passport name (₩1,111 authorization, not charged) or debit card (₩70,000 deposit, refunded when the device comes back in good condition) |
| Pick up / return | KT airport roaming centers | Incheon T1, T2, Gimpo or Gimhae airports |

Source: [KT — Wi-Fi router](https://roaming.kt.com/eng/router); [LG U+ — Pocket Wi-Fi](https://www.lguplus.com/korea-sim/eng/pc/product/pocket-wifi?tab=pocket-wifi); checked Oct 22, 2026.

> **Our take:** It's a good deal for a group that moves as one. The day you split up — one person shopping, the rest at a palace — whoever doesn't carry the router is offline. If that sounds like your trip, separate eSIMs are simpler.

## Free public Wi-Fi

![Seoul Station platform on Seoul Subway Line 4, with a yellow Way Out sign overhead](/img/photo-seoul-subway-platform.jpg?v=e8e0034c "Seoul Station, Subway Line 4, 2023. Photo: Mobius6 (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

VISITKOREA says free Wi-Fi is available in most public places, including airports, subway and train stations and some bus stops. Network names and sign-in steps vary by place. The national Public WiFi service — run with the three carriers in places like community centers, traditional markets and public buses — appears as **"Public WiFi Free"**: pick it, open your browser and tap the button to use the service. At airports and stations, use the network shown on the facility's signs or official website.

The Public WiFi service itself warns users not to handle sensitive personal information or make payments over it.

Source: [Public WiFi (Ministry of Science and ICT / NIA)](https://www.wififree.kr/pu/si/N01.do?language=en); [VISITKOREA](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140041); checked Oct 22, 2026.

> **Our take:** Treat free Wi-Fi as a backup. You need data most between stations — walking from the exit to your hotel with a map open — and you can't count on a hotspot along the way.

## So which one?

> **Our take:** If your phone takes an eSIM, is on the carrier's supported list and you just need data, buy a data eSIM online before you fly. If you need to make calls, or a specific app has to text you a code, pick a plan that says it supports that and have it switched on at the airport counter with your passport. Phone doesn't support eSIM? A physical SIM works if the phone is unlocked. Phone locked to your home carrier? Ask your carrier about unlocking, or rent a pocket Wi-Fi. A family that sticks together can share one router.

## Before you fly

1. Check that your phone supports eSIM, isn't carrier-locked and is on the Korean carrier's device list.
2. Decide: data only, or do you need calls or app codes?
3. Buy and install a data eSIM while you're on Wi-Fi — or reserve a SIM or pocket Wi-Fi for airport pickup.
4. Look at your home plan's roaming, so your home line doesn't run up charges. Apple suggests checking whether your carrier includes international roaming before you travel.
5. Install Naver Map — here's [how to use Naver Map in Korea](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/) — and plan your ride from [Incheon Airport to Seoul](/incheon-airport-to-seoul/).

## FAQ

### How much is an eSIM for Korea?

On the three Korean carriers' own sites, a 1-day LTE data eSIM costs ₩6,500 (checked Oct 22, 2026). KT lists 5 days at ₩27,500 and 30 days at ₩71,500.

### Can I get a Korean phone number as a tourist?

Yes. Some tourist plans include an 010 number — even KT's data-only eSIM, which can receive calls and texts after KT's airport entry check. To make calls or send texts, you need a Data + Voice plan; LG U+ and KT switch these on after a passport check at their airport counters.

### Do I need a Korean number for taxi or restaurant apps?

Not necessarily — a local number on its own isn't enough. LG U+ says app text verification works with its Voice/SMS plans, not with data only. Check that your chosen plan supports the app's verification method. For Korean banking or government identity checks, LG U+ says its plans aren't supported and KT says its eSIM doesn't support personal authentication.

### Is there free Wi-Fi in Korea?

Yes, at many airports, stations and public places. Network names vary; the national Public WiFi service appears as "Public WiFi Free". Avoid making payments on public Wi-Fi.

### Pocket Wi-Fi or eSIM?

A pocket Wi-Fi (₩4,400 a day at KT and LG U+) can be shared by a group but has to be returned at the airport. An eSIM stays on your phone and there's nothing to return.

## Sources

- Korea Tourism Organization (VISITKOREA) — Electricity & Communications (last updated Sep 11, 2026): https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140041
- LG U+ — Korea eSIM (Data): https://www.lguplus.com/korea-sim/eng/pc/product/esim?tab=data
- LG U+ — Korea SIM Card (Data + Voice): https://www.lguplus.com/korea-sim/eng/pc/product/simcard?tab=data-voice
- LG U+ — Pocket Wi-Fi: https://www.lguplus.com/korea-sim/eng/pc/product/pocket-wifi?tab=pocket-wifi
- SK Telecom — eSIM plans for visitors: https://www.skroaming.com/esim/esim
- KT — eSIM plans for visitors: https://roaming.kt.com/eng/esim
- KT — Wi-Fi router rental: https://roaming.kt.com/eng/router
- Public WiFi (Ministry of Science and ICT / NIA) — Service information: https://www.wififree.kr/pu/si/N01.do?language=en
- Apple Support — Use eSIM while traveling internationally with your iPhone: https://support.apple.com/en-us/118227

# How to Get a T-money Card in Korea (and Top It Up)

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/
Last checked: 2026-10-22

## Quick answer

- Buy a T-money card at a convenience store (GS25, CU, 7-Eleven, emart24 and others). Cards cost about ₩3,000–₩5,000 depending on the design — top it up before your first ride.
- Top it up with Korean won cash at the store counter or at subway station top-up machines.
- Tap your card when you get on and when you get off the bus, or you lose the transfer discount.

![Three steps to use T-money: buy at a convenience store, top up with Korean won cash, tap in and out on buses](/img/tmoney-steps.png?v=e2634456 "T-money in three steps. Prices and rules: see the sections below.")

## What is T-money?

T-money is Korea's rechargeable transit card. You load money onto it, tap it on the reader, and the fare comes off the balance. It also works outside Seoul — Busan's subway and buses accept it, for example — and on taxis. Transfer rules differ from city to city.

You don't *have* to use one: you can buy single-journey subway tickets at station machines — with cash, or with an overseas Visa or Mastercard at the newer machines on Lines 1–8 (about 3.7% card fee). But a card is cheaper on the subway, and you need one to get the transfer discount between buses and the subway.

| Seoul fare (adult, as of Oct 2026) | With T-money | Single ticket / cash |
|---|---|---|
| Subway, first 10 km | ₩1,550 | ₩1,650 |
| City bus — trunk (blue) or branch (green) | ₩1,500 | ₩1,500 |

Smaller green **local (village) buses** cost ₩1,200, and red rapid buses ₩3,000.

Source: Seoul Metropolitan Government — [subway fares](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/subway/) (in effect since June 28, 2025) and [bus fares](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/bus/); checked Oct 22, 2026.

Paying a bus fare in cash is getting harder: Seoul listed **183 cash-free bus routes** as of January 2026, so plan to pay buses with a card.

Source: [Seoul — cash-free bus routes](https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/archives/508898) (Korean), checked Oct 22, 2026.

## Where to buy a T-money card

The surest place is a **convenience store**. T-money lists GS25, CU, 7-Eleven, emart24, MINISTOP, Story Way and 365PLUS as sellers. Ask at the counter for a "T-money card".

- **Price: about ₩3,000–₩5,000**, depending on the design. Basic cards are ₩3,000 when the store has them.
- **The price is for the card only.** Top it up before your first ride.
- **The card price isn't included in balance refunds** — you only get back the money loaded on it.

Source: [T-money — card types and prices](https://pay.tmoney.co.kr/ncs/pct/tmnyintd/ReadTmnyIntd.dev?cardGdKndCd=01), [T-money guide for foreign visitors](https://pay.tmoney.co.kr/ncs/pct/ugd/ReadFrgnGd.dev) and [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140663); checked Oct 22, 2026.

The Korea Tourism Organization says information centers in Seoul subway stations on Lines 1–8 also sell cards, but T-money's own guide for visitors lists subway stations as top-up points only. A convenience store is the surest bet.

> **Local tip:** Convenience stores both sell and top up T-money at the counter, so you can buy the card and load it in a single visit before your first ride.

## How to top it up

Top-ups at convenience stores and subway station machines are made with **Korean won cash**. You can top up:

- at any convenience store counter that sells T-money — hand over the card and the cash, and say how much you want to add
- at the top-up machines and information centers in subway stations

The rules:

- ₩1,000 to ₩90,000 per top-up, in ₩1,000 steps
- A card can hold up to ₩500,000

Source: [T-money guide for foreign visitors](https://pay.tmoney.co.kr/ncs/pct/ugd/ReadFrgnGd.dev), checked Oct 22, 2026.

> **Our take:** For a typical city trip, ₩20,000–₩30,000 at a time is plenty. Topping up in smaller amounts means less money stuck on the card when you leave.

## How transfers work (and how to save money)

In Seoul, when you switch between the subway and a bus, or between two buses, the trip is charged as one journey instead of a new base fare for each ride (extra distance charges can still apply). To get it:

1. **Tap the card when you get on and when you get off the bus.** In Seoul, tapping off is required for the transfer discount.
2. Make the transfer **within 30 minutes** of getting off — or **within 60 minutes between 9 pm and 7 am**.
3. Re-boarding the **same bus route** doesn't count as a transfer.
4. One trip can include up to **four transfers (five rides)**.

Source: [Seoul Metropolitan Government](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/bus/), checked Oct 22, 2026.

## Mistakes to avoid

- **Not tapping off the bus.** Your next ride is then charged as a new trip instead of a discounted transfer.
- **Tapping your whole wallet.** With several contactless cards together, the reader may not read the right one. Take the T-money card out and tap it on its own.
- **Loading too much at the end of your trip.** Some refund points charge a fee, and larger balances are hard for visitors to refund (see below).

## Getting your money back before you fly home

![Where to refund a T-money balance: convenience stores for balances up to the store limit with a ₩500 fee, T-money Town for larger balances](/img/tmoney-refund.png?v=a4cb9615 "Refund options at a glance. Details and conditions are in the table below.")

You can cash out the money left on the card:

| Where | What you can refund | Fee |
|---|---|---|
| A convenience store that sells T-money | Balances up to the store's limit: GS25 under ₩20,000 · 7-Eleven ₩20,000 or less · CU and emart24 ₩30,000 or less | ₩500 |
| T-money Town (Seoul Station Exit 10, Seoul City Tower 1F) | Also balances above a store's limit — including amounts of ₩50,000 or less | No fee for refunds up to ₩500,000 a month in total; 1% above that |

At T-money Town:

- Refunds of **₩50,000 or more** require an identity check (name, date of birth and contact details).
- Refunds of **₩100,000 or more** are paid into a **Korean bank account** after 6 pm on the next business day (not weekends or public holidays). Bring ID and a copy of your bankbook for this.

Bank ATM refunds also exist, but they need a Korean bank account in your own name. Check the official refund rules before you go.

If you don't have a Korean bank account, keep your balance low near the end of your trip.

Source: [T-money refund rules](https://pay.tmoney.co.kr/ncs/pct/ugd/ReadNrmlCardRyGd.dev) (Korean), checked Oct 22, 2026.

> **Our take:** Plan your last top-up so only a few thousand won is left when you head to the airport, then use it up on the way. The AREX All-stop train to Incheon Airport accepts T-money (see [Incheon Airport to Seoul](/incheon-airport-to-seoul/) for routes and fares). Airport Limousine also says you can pay with T-money on its buses going **to** the airport (not from the airport, where you buy a ticket first) — other bus operators may differ.

## Using T-money outside Seoul

T-money also works outside Seoul. In **Busan**, it's accepted on the subway and buses, and bus–subway transfers within 30 minutes are discounted. Seoul's transfer rules don't automatically apply elsewhere — check the local rules. Busan's subway fare with a card is ₩1,600–₩1,800 depending on distance (as listed by Busan Transportation Corporation).

Source: [Busan Transportation Corporation](https://www.humetro.busan.kr/homepage/english/page/subLocation.do?menu_no=100601040101), checked Oct 22, 2026.

## Paying for taxis

Taxis in Korea generally accept cash, credit cards and transit cards such as T-money.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Taxis](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140661), checked Oct 22, 2026.

## T-money or a Climate Card pass?

If you'll spend most of your trip in Seoul, Seoul's **Climate Card short-term pass** is the main alternative. It gives unlimited rides for a set number of days:

| Pass | Price |
|---|---|
| 1 day | ₩5,000 |
| 2 days | ₩8,000 |
| 3 days | ₩10,000 |
| 5 days | ₩15,000 |
| 7 days | ₩20,000 |

Source: [Seoul Metropolitan Government — Climate Card](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/climate-card/), checked Oct 22, 2026.

The physical card costs ₩3,000 extra. The pass starts on the day you load it, and a 1-day pass lasts until that day's last bus or subway — not 24 hours. You can pay for these passes with an overseas Visa or Mastercard — since March 17, 2026 also at 440 new ticket machines on Seoul Subway Lines 1–8 (about 3.7% card fee).

What it **doesn't** cover: the Sinbundang Line, subway lines outside Seoul, buses not licensed by Seoul, airport and intercity buses, and taxis. At Incheon Airport you can only **get off** with it — you can't board the AREX train there. Coverage changed on **October 1, 2026** — several Gyeonggi Province sections were removed — so check the [official FAQ](https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/public/climatecard-faq/faq-short) (Korean) before you buy.

> **Our take:** Do the quick math for your own trip first. One example, with its assumptions spelled out: you **already have a T-money card**, you **don't have a Climate Card yet** (so you pay ₩3,000 for it), and each trip would otherwise cost a basic fare with T-money (₩1,550 subway or ₩1,500 city bus). Then a 3-day pass (₩10,000 + ₩3,000 = ₩13,000) pays off only if you make **9 or more** separate trips in those three days. If you already own a Climate Card, you pay just ₩10,000 and it pays off from **7** trips. If you'd be buying both cards new, or you're also heading to Busan or other cities, the answer changes — run your own numbers.

## FAQ

### Can I use T-money outside Seoul?

Yes — for example, Busan's subway and buses accept it. Note that the AREX Express airport train needs a separate ticket.

### Can I top up T-money with a credit card?

Not for regular T-money top-ups at convenience stores and subway stations — those are made with Korean won cash. Climate Card passes and single-journey subway tickets can be bought with an overseas Visa or Mastercard at the newer machines on Seoul Subway Lines 1–8.

### Can I get the ₩3,000 card price back?

No. Refunds cover only the money left on the card. Convenience stores charge ₩500; T-money Town lists no fee for refunds up to ₩500,000 a month in total (1% above that).

### Need help in English?

Call the **1330 Korea Travel Helpline** (+82-2-1330 from a foreign phone) for help in English and several other languages.

## Sources

- T-money — Refund rules (Korean): https://pay.tmoney.co.kr/ncs/pct/ugd/ReadNrmlCardRyGd.dev
- Seoul Metropolitan Government — Subway fares and transfers: https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/subway/
- Seoul Metropolitan Government — Bus fares and transfers: https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/bus/
- Seoul Metropolitan Government — Climate Card: https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/climate-card/
- Seoul Climate Card FAQ, short-term passes (Korean, updated Oct 2026): https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/public/climatecard-faq/faq-short
- Korea Tourism Organization — Transportation cards: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140663
- Korea Tourism Organization — Taxis: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140661
- Busan Transportation Corporation — Fares: https://www.humetro.busan.kr/homepage/english/page/subLocation.do?menu_no=100601040101
- Busan Transportation Corporation — Transfers: https://www2.humetro.busan.kr/homepage/english/page/subLocation.do?menu_no=100601040201

# How to Use Naver Map in Korea (and Why Google Maps Isn't Enough)

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/
Last checked: 2026-10-22

## Quick answer

- Use Naver Map in Korea. It has English maps, English navigation, and transit, walking and driving directions.
- Google Maps showed transit routes in Seoul in our web test on Oct 22, 2026, but no walking or driving directions for the route we checked.
- Install Naver Map before you fly. It follows your phone's language, or you can pick English in the app's language setting.

![Comparison of Google Maps and Naver Map in Korea for transit, walking and driving directions, based on our Oct 22, 2026 test and Naver Map's store listing](/img/naver-compare.png?v=51b5d6bf "Google Maps vs Naver Map in Korea. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | Google Maps | Naver Map |
|---|---|---|
| Transit directions | ✅ Worked in our test | ✅ With real-time departure and arrival times |
| Walking directions | ❌ Not available in our test | ✅ |
| Driving directions | ❌ Not available in our test | ✅ English navigation |
| Map languages | — | English, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese |

Source: our Google Maps test on Oct 22, 2026; [Naver Map App Store listing](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/naver-map-navigation/id311867728), checked Oct 22, 2026.

## Why Google Maps isn't enough in Korea

On Oct 22, 2026, we asked Google Maps (on the web, in English) for directions from Seoul Station to Gyeongbokgung Palace:

- **Transit:** route options were shown; travel times varied by departure time.
- **Walking:** *"Sorry, your search appears to be outside our current coverage area for walking."*
- **Driving:** the same message, *"…outside our current coverage area for driving."*
- **Cycling:** the cycling option was unavailable in that web test.

That's one route on one day, on the web version, and it may change. On **February 27, 2026**, South Korea's government conditionally approved Google's request to export 1:5,000-scale map data, subject to security requirements. That decision doesn't by itself tell you when new features arrive — in our web test almost eight months later, walking and driving directions were still unavailable for the route we checked.

Source: our own test, Oct 22, 2026; [Korea Policy Briefing — Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport](https://www.korea.kr/news/policyNewsView.do?newsId=148960112) (Korean), Feb 27, 2026.

## What Naver Map gives you

Naver Map is made by NAVER Corp. According to its App Store listing and NAVER's own announcements:

- **Maps in four languages** — English, Japanese, Korean and Simplified Chinese — and **English navigation**.
- **Transit directions** for different kinds of transport, with **real-time departure and arrival times**.
- **Walking directions** and **car navigation** with real-time traffic.
- **Translated place information**: NAVER says it has extended English, Chinese and Japanese translation to visitor reviews and place filters, and improved translations of place pages and transit details.

Source: [Naver Map App Store listing](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/naver-map-navigation/id311867728); NAVER press releases of [Oct 2, 2024](https://navercorp.com/media/pressReleasesDetail?seq=32066) (Korean) and [Dec 30, 2024](https://www.navercorp.com/en/media/pressReleasesDetail?seq=32212); checked Oct 22, 2026.

## How to use Naver Map, step by step

![Naver Map in four steps: install the app from NAVER Corp., use English, search for a place, and get transit, walking or car directions](/img/naver-steps.png?v=533ba430 "Naver Map in four steps. Details below.")

### 1. Install the right app

Search your app store for **"NAVER Map"** and check that the developer is **NAVER Corp.** (the App Store lists it as "NAVER Maps, Navigation"). Install it before you fly.

### 2. Get it in English

NAVER says the multilingual version follows **your phone's language setting**, or the **language setting inside the Naver Map app**. If your phone is set to English, the map should appear in English; if not, look for the language option in the app's settings and choose English.

### 3. Search for a place

Type the place you want to go. Place pages, visitor reviews and filters can appear in English, according to NAVER's announcements.

> **Local tip:** If an English search doesn't find the place you want, try searching with its Korean name or address — for example, copied from the place's website or your booking confirmation.

### 4. Get directions

Choose your destination and pick how you're traveling:

- **Transit** — shows routes with real-time departure and arrival times
- **Walking** — walking directions
- **Car** — navigation with real-time traffic, with English navigation available

### 5. Save the places you'll need

To save places, **sign in with a NAVER account**. Search for your hotel or another place, then use the star/save button. If you prefer not to sign in, keep your hotel's name and address in a note and search for it when you need it.

Source: [Naver Map App Store listing](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/naver-map-navigation/id311867728); NAVER press release of [Oct 2, 2024](https://navercorp.com/media/pressReleasesDetail?seq=32066) and [NAVER Map Help — saving places](https://help.naver.com/service/5637/contents/692?lang=ko&osType=COMMONOS) (Korean); checked Oct 22, 2026.

> **Our take:** For a first trip to Korea, install Naver Map even if you love Google Maps. Use Google Maps for places you've already saved if you like, but let Naver Map handle the walking part — from the subway exit to the door.

## Before you fly: checklist

1. **Install Naver Map** and set it to English.
2. **Sign in to save your hotel** and first few stops — or keep their names and addresses in a note.
3. **Plan how you'll get online** in Korea (eSIM, SIM card or Wi-Fi) so the app can load routes.
4. **Read up on getting around:** [Incheon Airport to Seoul](/incheon-airport-to-seoul/) and [how to get a T-money card](/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/).

## FAQ

### Does Google Maps work in South Korea?

Partly. In our test on Oct 22, 2026, it gave transit directions in Seoul but no walking or driving directions.

### Is Naver Map available in English?

Yes. Its App Store listing lists English, Japanese, Korean and Simplified Chinese maps, plus English navigation.

### How do I switch Naver Map to English?

NAVER says the app follows your phone's language setting, or you can choose a language in the Naver Map app's own language setting.

### Did Korea allow Google Maps to work fully in 2026?

On February 27, 2026, the government conditionally approved Google's request to export 1:5,000-scale map data, subject to security requirements. In our web test on Oct 22, 2026, walking and driving directions were still unavailable for the route we checked.

# Incheon Airport to Seoul: AREX Train vs Airport Bus vs Taxi

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/incheon-airport-to-seoul/
Last checked: 2026-10-22

## Quick answer

- Cheapest: AREX All-stop train with a T-money card — about ₩4,750 (T1) or ₩5,350 (T2) to Seoul Station, around 1 hour.
- Fastest to Seoul Station: AREX Express — ₩13,000; 43 min between Seoul Station and T1, 51 min to T2. Buy a separate ticket before boarding.
- With heavy luggage: airport limousine bus (₩16,000–₩17,000 for adults on Airport Limousine's Seoul routes; other operators vary) or a taxi. Arriving late? Night buses (route numbers start with N) and taxis run when trains and regular buses have finished.

## The short version

![Comparison of AREX All-stop train, AREX Express, limousine bus and taxi from Incheon Airport by adult fare, travel time and payment](/img/airport-compare.png?v=2e087b2c "Four ways from Incheon Airport to Seoul at a glance.")

| Option | Adult fare | Time to central Seoul | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| AREX All-stop train | ₩4,750 (T1) / ₩5,350 (T2) to Seoul Station, by transit card | About 59 min (T1) / 66 min (T2) to Seoul Station | Budget travelers, Hongdae and Mapo area |
| AREX Express train | ₩13,000 | 43 min (T1) / 51 min (T2) to Seoul Station | Getting to Seoul Station fast |
| Airport limousine bus | ₩17,000 (direct) / ₩16,000 (via Gimpo Airport), Airport Limousine routes | Depends on route and traffic | Heavy luggage, hotels near a bus stop |
| Taxi | Metered, plus tolls | Depends on traffic | Groups, families, late arrivals |

Source: [AREX All-stop fares](https://www.airportrailroad.com/train/normal/fare), [AREX Express](https://www.airportrailroad.com/train/express/introduce), [Airport Limousine](https://www.airportlimousine.co.kr/sub/sub02_01.php) and [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140654) — adult fares, checked Oct 22, 2026.

First, check your ticket for **Terminal 1 (T1) or Terminal 2 (T2)**. Train fares and times are different from each terminal. If you need to switch terminals, free shuttle buses connect them — route 03 runs from T2 to T1 every 7–20 minutes (4:30 am–11:35 pm) and route 04 from T1 to T2 every 10–20 minutes (4:30 am–11:20 pm); allow time for waiting as well as the ride. The AREX train takes about 6 minutes (₩1,200 for adults with a transit card).

## Option 1: AREX All-stop train (cheapest)

The All-stop train is a regular commuter train that runs from the airport into Seoul, stopping at stations like **Gimpo Airport, Digital Media City, Hongik Univ. (Hongdae), Gongdeok and Seoul Station**.

- **Pay with T-money** — just tap in at the gate. (If you don't have a card yet, see [how to get a T-money card](/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/). Single-journey cards cost ₩100 more, plus a ₩500 deposit you get back at your destination.)
- **Fares from T1 / T2 (adult, transit card):**

| To | From T1 | From T2 |
|---|---|---|
| Seoul Station | ₩4,750 | ₩5,350 |
| Hongik Univ. | ₩4,650 | ₩5,250 |
| Gongdeok | ₩4,650 | ₩5,250 |
| Gimpo Airport | ₩4,350 | ₩4,950 |

Source: [AREX All-stop fares](https://www.airportrailroad.com/train/normal/fare), checked Oct 22, 2026.

- **Time:** about 59 minutes between Seoul Station and T1, and 66 minutes to T2 (some trains take 2–6 minutes longer).
- Check the current AREX timetable for the last All-stop train from your terminal to your destination. AREX's timetable revision effective October 23, 2026 also affects some All-stop departures.
- You can transfer to the Seoul subway at stations like Hongik Univ., Gongdeok and Seoul Station.

> **Local tip:** If you're staying around Hongdae or Mapo, the All-stop train gets you there without changing — and it's cheaper than the Express, which only goes to Seoul Station.

## Option 2: AREX Express train (fastest to Seoul Station)

The Express connects Seoul Station, Terminal 1 and Terminal 2. It runs **non-stop between Terminal 1 and Seoul Station**; trains from Terminal 2 call at Terminal 1 first.

- **Fare:** ₩13,000 for adults, ₩9,500 for children (ages 6–12).
- **Time:** 43 minutes between Seoul Station and T1, 51 minutes to T2 (time on the train, not including walking or waiting).
- **You need a separate Express ticket** — buy it before boarding at the Express Train Customer Center (B1 of the Transportation Center at T1 and T2) or online on the AREX website in advance.
- AREX's revised Express timetable is effective from **October 23, 2026**. Check the [official timetable](https://www.airportrailroad.com/train/express/info) for your travel date, departure terminal and direction before planning around a train.

Source: [AREX Express](https://www.airportrailroad.com/train/express/introduce), checked Oct 22, 2026.

> **Our take:** The Express makes most sense if your hotel is near Seoul Station or you're catching a KTX train from there. For most other neighborhoods, you'll still need to transfer to the subway, so the time saved over the All-stop train is smaller than it looks.

## Option 3: Airport limousine bus

Limousine buses run from the airport to many parts of Seoul. Check the route list for the stop closest to where you're staying.

- **Fare (Airport Limousine's Seoul routes):** adults ₩17,000 on direct routes and ₩16,000 on routes via Gimpo Airport; children (elementary-school age) ₩12,000. Other bus operators' fares may differ.
- **Buy a ticket before boarding** at the bus ticket counters or ticket machines. Don't count on paying cash or T-money on the bus when leaving the airport.
- **Going back to the airport?** Airport Limousine says you can pay with cash or T-money on its buses in that direction (not with a regular credit card or a Climate Card). Other operators may differ.
- **T1 ticket counters:** 1st floor arrivals hall, near the exit gates.
- **T2 ticket counters:** B1, Transportation Center.
- Ticket machines run 24 hours.
- Journey time depends on the route and traffic.

Source: [Airport Limousine — fares](https://www.airportlimousine.co.kr/sub/sub02_01.php), [ticket counters](https://www.airportlimousine.co.kr/sub/sub02_02.php) and [payment FAQ](https://www.airportlimousine.co.kr/sub/sub03_02.php) (Korean), checked Oct 22, 2026.

> **Our take:** If there's a limousine stop near your hotel, the bus saves you from carrying big suitcases through subway transfers. Check the walking distance from the stop to your hotel before you choose it.

## Option 4: Taxi

Use the **official taxi stands** outside the arrivals hall (1st floor at both terminals). The airport warns travelers not to use touts who approach you inside the terminal. There are separate stands for Seoul, Gyeonggi and Incheon taxis — for central Seoul, follow the signs to the **Seoul taxi** stand. The rates below are for Seoul taxis.

**Metered taxis (Seoul rates):**

| Type | Base fare | Then |
|---|---|---|
| Regular | ₩4,800 for the first 1.6 km | ₩100 per 131 m — in slow traffic, time is charged too (₩100 per 30 seconds) |
| Deluxe / SUV / van | ₩7,000 for the first 3 km | ₩200 per 151 m — in slow traffic, ₩200 per 36 seconds |

Source: [Seoul Metropolitan Government](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/taxi/) — rates in effect since Feb 1, 2023; checked Oct 22, 2026.

- **Tolls are added on top of the meter.**
- **Late-night surcharge (regular taxis):** +20% from 10 pm to 11 pm, +40% from 11 pm to 2 am, +20% from 2 am to 4 am. Deluxe taxis add 20% from 10 pm to 4 am.

**International Taxi:** International Taxi has fixed zone fares between Incheon Airport and Seoul — ₩70,000–₩95,000 for a sedan and ₩100,000–₩140,000 for an SUV, van or deluxe car, depending on the zone of your destination. Book at least 24 hours ahead; for help on the day, ask at an airport information desk.

Source: [Seoul Metropolitan Government — International taxi section fares](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/taxi/) and [International Taxi](https://www.intltaxi.co.kr), checked Oct 22, 2026.

> **Our take:** For a group of three or four with luggage, a taxi is worth pricing out — four adult limousine tickets already cost ₩64,000–₩68,000, and a taxi drops you at your address. With four people and big suitcases, check that the car is large enough. For one or two people, the train or bus is much cheaper.

## Landing late at night?

Check the last train and regular airport bus for your terminal and destination before you fly — last departures differ by route and terminal. If those services have finished:

- **Night buses** run from the airport to Seoul. Their route numbers start with **"N"** (for example N6000, N6002 and N6701 from T1), and adult fares on these routes are ₩17,000–₩18,000. Buy tickets in advance at the bus ticket counters or machines. Departure times are limited, so check the airport's late-night bus timetable for your terminal before you fly ([T1](https://www.airport.kr/ap_ko/979/subview.do) · [T2](https://www.airport.kr/ap_ko/982/subview.do), Korean).
- **Taxis** wait at the official stands — remember the late-night surcharge.

Source: [Incheon Airport — late-night buses from T1](https://www.airport.kr/ap_ko/979/subview.do) (Korean) and [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140654), checked Oct 22, 2026.

## Using a Climate Card pass from the airport?

Seoul's **Climate Card short-term pass** (unlimited Seoul subway and bus rides) lets you **get off** at the Incheon Airport T1 and T2 stations, but you **can't board** the train there with it. This has been the rule since September 13, 2024, and Seoul restated it in its October 1, 2026 coverage update. So you can use it on your way *to* the airport, but not for your first ride into Seoul — pay for that ride with T-money or a ticket.

Source: [Seoul Metropolitan Government — Climate Card](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/climate-card/) and [Climate Card FAQ](https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/public/climatecard-faq/faq-short) (Korean, updated Oct 1, 2026), checked Oct 22, 2026.

## FAQ

### Can I use T-money on the AREX Express?

The Express requires a separate ticket bought before boarding. T-money works on the All-stop train.

### Does the train stop at Gimpo Airport?

Only the All-stop train stops at Gimpo Airport. The Express serves Terminal 2, Terminal 1 and Seoul Station, running non-stop between Terminal 1 and Seoul Station.

### How do I get between Terminal 1 and Terminal 2?

Take the free terminal shuttle bus (route 03 from T2 to T1, every 7–20 minutes, 4:30 am–11:35 pm; route 04 from T1 to T2, every 10–20 minutes, 4:30 am–11:20 pm), or the AREX train (about 6 minutes; ₩1,200 for adults with a transit card, ₩1,300 with a single-journey card, plus a ₩500 deposit you get back).

### I'm stuck — who can help in English?

Call the **1330 Korea Travel Helpline** (+82-2-1330 from a foreign phone) for help in English and several other languages, or ask at the airport information desks in the arrivals hall.
